summary: On node1, /tmp and /dev/shm are now mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev via persistent /etc/fstab tmpfs entries. Verified enforcement before and after a full node reboot (boot_id changed, confirming genuine restart), including blocked script execution and blocked device-node access.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline mount state: /tmp was part of rootfs (not a separate mount); /dev/shm was tmpfs with only nosuid,nodev (no noexec)
Backed up /etc/fstab and appended two tmpfs entries: '/tmp tmpfs defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev 0 0' and '/dev/shm tmpfs defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev 0 0'
Applied changes live: 'mount -o remount /dev/shm' and 'mount /tmp', confirmed via findmnt that both show nosuid,nodev,noexec

Falsification test pre-reboot: created executable script in /tmp (blocked, permission denied, exit 126); created device node with mknod in /tmp and /dev/shm and attempted to read it with dd (blocked, permission denied)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id 901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a, uptime since 2026-09-29 11:12:18, healthy mount options confirmed
Issued reboot via backgrounded 'nohup sh -c "sleep 2 && reboot"' so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until command execution resumed; observed connection timeout/reset during the restart window
Confirmed changed boot identity post-restart: boot_id cfe6cf8b-d967-46f6-81f1-d7f1801dc73a, new uptime since 2026-09-29 11:13:02

Post-restart verification: findmnt shows /tmp and /dev/shm both persisted with nosuid,nodev,noexec from fstab; re-ran exec and device-node tests, both blocked as expected, confirming persistence across reboot

evidence.requirement: Baseline: original /tmp and /dev/shm mount state before hardening
evidence.summary: findmnt showed /tmp was not a separate mount (rootfs) and /dev/shm lacked noexec; fstab had no prior /tmp or /dev/shm entries

evidence.requirement: fstab modified with persistent noexec,nosuid,nodev options for /tmp and /dev/shm
evidence.summary: Backed up fstab and appended tmpfs entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev

evidence.requirement: Options applied live and mounts show noexec,nosuid,nodev
evidence.summary: mount -o remount /dev/shm and mount /tmp succeeded; findmnt confirms rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec on both

evidence.requirement: Execution and device-node access are actually blocked (falsification proof)
evidence.summary: Chmod+x script on /tmp failed to execute (permission denied, exit 126); mknod succeeded but dd read of the device node failed with permission denied, proving nodev is enforced

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline with boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a, uptime since 11:12:18, and healthy /tmp and /dev/shm mount options plus fstab entries
Backgrounded delayed reboot command returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node restart in progress / node unreachable during reboot
evidence.summary: Subsequent polls returned connection timeout then connection reset, consistent with the node rebooting

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving a genuine restart occurred
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a to cfe6cf8b-d967-46f6-81f1-d7f1801dc73a with new uptime since 11:13:02

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: mount options persisted and enforcement still active
evidence.summary: findmnt shows /tmp and /dev/shm still have nosuid,nodev,noexec after reboot; re-ran exec and device-node tests, both blocked, confirming settings survived reboot via fstab
